title: Approximation of finitely presented algebra maps modulo the ideal
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] with $A$ a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Let $R$ be a finitely presented commutative $A$-algebra (a quotient of $A[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ by a finitely generated ideal), and let $c:R\to\widehat A$ be an $A$-algebra map to the $I$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then there exists an $A$-algebra map $\sigma:R\to A$ such that $\pi\circ\sigma=p\circ c$, where $\pi:A\to A/I$ is the quotient map and $p:\widehat A\to A/I$ is the completion projection.

proof.text: Choose a polynomial algebra surjecting onto R with finitely generated kernel by Algebra.FinitePresentation.out, Mathlib/RingTheory/FinitePresentation.lean:44–45. Enumerate a finite generating set of its kernel with a Fin type. The images of the variables under c solve these relations because the surjection kills them.

Apply henselian_pair_approximation with N=1 to the relations and the completed images. Evaluation at the resulting elements of A kills each relation, hence the whole kernel. Descend evaluation through the surjection by AlgHom.liftOfSurjective, Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Operations.lean:562–565. This gives sigma:R to A.

The kernel of the completion projection is the extended ideal; its composite with A to the completion is the quotient map. Apply these equalities to the congruences on the variables. Both A-algebra maps into A/I therefore agree on all variables and constants, hence on the polynomial algebra. Surjectivity of the presentation gives equality on R.
